name: Learn a basic 12-bar blues
blurb: The most useful twelve bars in music. Learn the form once and you can jam with strangers, on guitar, piano or harmonica, for the rest of your life.
steps: Learn the form: four bars of I, two of IV, two of I, one of V, one of IV, two of I. Count it out loud until it is instinctive.
Play it in one key with basic chords, keeping strict time throughout.
Learn the shuffle rhythm, which is what makes it sound like blues rather than a chord exercise.
Learn the minor pentatonic scale in the same key and play simple phrases over the changes.
Learn to leave space. Beginner soloing is too many notes; the form rewards phrases with gaps.
Play along with a backing track without losing your place in the form.
tips: Losing the form is the classic error. Count the bars even while soloing.
Learn it in two keys — E and A on guitar, C and F on piano — and you can join almost any jam.
proof: You play the full twelve bars, in time, over a backing track, and take a short solo without losing the form.
